venue: The Coca-Cola Roxy, The Battery Atlanta, GA
blurb: Trippie Redd is coming to the Coca-Cola Roxy on Monday the 24th, right before Thanksgiving week heats up. If you're in that mid-20s to early-30s range and have been following his catalog, this is a good excuse to get out before the holiday chaos takes over. The Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta and The Battery makes the whole night easy, with parking and plenty of options for dinner before the show. Check the Know Before You Go page on the Roxy's site before you head out.
scoring_notes: Trippie Redd skews younger than the median Perimeter audience (age 38), but the audience has enough young professionals in the mix to make this relevant. The Battery location is squarely in the coverage zone. Uniqueness is solid — a specific artist, one night only. Demographic fit is the main question mark; this is a pick for the younger end of the Perimeter readership.

event_name: The Nutcracker — Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre
venue: Jennie T. Anderson Theatre, Marietta, GA
blurb: Thanksgiving afternoon, the family is around, and you need something to do with the next few hours before the second round of food. Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre's production of The Nutcracker is a genuinely nice option — live dance, holiday atmosphere, the kind of thing that actually holds a family's attention across ages. The Jennie T. Anderson Theatre in Marietta is a solid venue and this is Thanksgiving weekend, so if you're going, don't wait on tickets.
scoring_notes: The Nutcracker runs every year so uniqueness is moderate, but the Thanksgiving timing and family-friendly format make it relevant for this audience's mix of young families and empty nesters. Slight distance from Perimeter core but within range. Good fit as a Thanksgiving day activity. Not a standout pick on its own but fills a real use case for the audience.

venue: C. Ellet's, The Battery Atlanta, GA
blurb: Saturday morning with nowhere to be, a live jazz duo, Southern fried chicken, and a mimosa in hand at C. Ellet's. This is a weekly thing but that doesn't make it less worth doing, especially heading into Thanksgiving week when a slow, good brunch at The Battery sounds about right. The jazz duo plays from 11 to 3 every Saturday and Sunday. Make a reservation, go with someone you like talking to, and take your time.
scoring_notes: Recurring weekly event, so uniqueness is low. That said, it's a legitimate experience at a well-known Battery restaurant that fits the adult-leaning Perimeter audience well. Good fallback option. The timing right before Thanksgiving makes it contextually relevant as a 'treat yourself' pick heading into the holiday. Strong demographic fit for empty nesters and young professionals.

blurb: It's a free outdoor festival in Roswell with gourmet food trucks, craft drinks, live music, DJ sets, and college football on big screens all afternoon. The Fall and Flavor Festival at You42 Studios is a genuinely easy yes for a Saturday where you want to get out of the house but don't want to plan too hard. Bring the family, bring friends, eat something interesting, and catch whatever game is on. It's right at the top of the Perimeter coverage area and it won't cost you a thing to walk in.
scoring_notes: Free entry is appealing but not the main draw — the combination of food trucks, live music, and game day screens makes it genuinely multi-use for this audience. Roswell is on the northern edge of the coverage area but reachable. Good fit for young families and young professionals. Uniqueness is moderate since outdoor food festivals are common, but the timing right before Thanksgiving week gives it seasonal relevance.

venue: Park Bench, The Battery Atlanta, GA
blurb: Black Friday night, no cover, two pianists playing off each other and off the crowd, right at The Battery. This is exactly what you want after a full day of family. Dueling Pianos at Park Bench is the kind of show where the setlist depends on who's in the room and what they're asking for — it's loud, it's fun, and it moves fast. General seating fills up, so grab a table reservation if you want to actually sit down. Walk in otherwise and see what happens. Either way, it's a good night.
scoring_notes: The Battery is a natural Perimeter destination. No-cover entry plays well for spontaneous post-Thanksgiving plans. Adult-skewing event fits the audience well. Uniqueness is moderate since Dueling Pianos runs regularly, but the holiday timing and 'Holiday Kickoff' framing make this iteration relevant. Strong audience match for the young professionals and empty nesters in the mix.

blurb: If you grew up with Journey on the radio, this one is worth the drive to Marietta. DEPARTURE has been doing this for 18 years and they're considered the best Journey tribute band in the country, which isn't a small claim. The lead vocalist matches Steve Perry note for note, everything you hear is played live, and they run through two full sets of the hits. VIP gets you a meet and greet, drink tickets, a signed poster, and a mini concert starting at 6:30. The Strand is a beautiful old theater, it's Black Friday night, and Don't Stop Believin' is going to sound really good right now. Grab your tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Journey's core fanbase maps well to the 38 median age and older end of the Perimeter audience. The Strand is a beloved venue with regional pull. The 18-year track record and national reputation give this credibility beyond a typical tribute act. Black Friday night timing is a genuine selling point. Slight distance from core Perimeter coverage but well within reasonable drive. VIP experience adds a premium tier that works for the $105K HHI.

event_name: BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience at Truist Park
blurb: Black Friday plans just got a serious upgrade. This one is genuinely one-of-a-kind: you and up to five others get a behind-the-scenes tour of the Atlanta Braves clubhouse, batting cages, and dugout, plus the chance to play catch on the field. BLOOPER shows up in full holiday mode, there's a festive photo op, and you walk away with a photo next to the NL East Pennant. If you've got kids who love the Braves, this is not a thing you can replicate on a random Saturday. It's holiday-exclusive, it's inside a stadium most people never see from that angle, and it's the kind of morning that beats another lap around a mall by a mile.
scoring_notes: Truist Park is in the Perimeter audience's backyard. The holiday-exclusive access angle is genuinely unique — this isn't a standard stadium tour. Strong pull for young families and young professionals with kids. The $105K median HHI means ticket price is a non-issue. Uniqueness score is a 10 because behind-the-scenes clubhouse access on a holiday weekend is not something you stumble into.
